Definition: from G1722 and τυλίσσω (to twist; probably akin to G1507); to entwine, i.e. wind up in:--wrap in (together).
BiblicalUsage: To wrap up, to wind in cloth. Joseph wrapped Jesus' body in a clean linen cloth in Matthew 27:59 and laid it in the tomb in Luke 23:53, and on the morning of the resurrection the napkin that had been about His head lay wrapped together in a place by itself in John 20:7.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the folded napkin is the quietest proof of the resurrection — no thief folds the grave-clothes, and no grave-robber leaves things tidy. I hold that the linen that wrapped a dead body now testifies that the body is gone because He lives.
RelatedEvents: The Burial of Jesus; The Resurrection
